verdict.rationale: Vue's official Suspense guide documents a built-in <Suspense> component that renders a loading state through #fallback slots while nested async setup() and async components resolve. That covers the suspense half of the story. However, Vue flags <Suspense> as experimental with an API that may change, and the evidence shows no dedicated resource primitive that turns server-loaded data into reactive state. missing for 10: a documented resource/data-loading primitive that exposes fetched data as reactive state, stable (non-experimental) Suspense status, independent hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a developer, I can treat server-loaded data as reactive state and build a responsive loading UI for it using resource and suspense primitives

citations.quote: <Suspense> is a built-in component for orchestrating async dependencies in a component tree. It can render a loading state while waiting for multiple nested async dependencies down the component tree to be resolved.
<Suspense> is an experimental feature. It is not guaranteed to reach stable status and the API may change before it does.
